transcript: Well, we could see Boop on tour. In the national tour news, we got the Broadway in Atlanta season announced today. These are our first tour dates for buena vista Social Club, Boop, and Operation Mincemeat. Really excited to see how all three of these translate to a tour production. Operation mincemeat is definitely one of those shows that's really intimate on Broadway and in the West End. I'm curious how it plays to these larger spaces. But it's such a fun show that I think audiences will really like it as long as it plays to the back of that balcony. Buena vista Social Club. I think it's gonna be an incredible tour. Just the design of the show, the dancing of that show, and of course, the musicians are really, really, really going to get to shine in these larger spaces as long. As long as the sound mixing is there, which sometimes can be a challenge when you're going to a new space. But I. I really think it's gonna play well in tours. And honestly, I think Boop is going to play better on tour than it did on Broadway. I think it's the kind of show that is perfect for a tour audience. Of course, not having Jasmine Amy Rogers on tour is going to be a huge loss, but I saw the Broadway production without Jasmine, and Tori Byrd was also incredible. And I think that really, whoever they Get in. That role is going to be a star in the making. I cannot wait to see that cast. All of the set pieces that I can recall are going to be able to tour easily, so there's not a lot of translating that they need to do there. And the big dance numbers are going to be gorgeous in these big auditoriums. We also have new dates for Death Becomes Her, another tour I'm really excited for. And water for elephants and the notebook, two of my favourite national tours from last year. And then we have some older shows that are continuing on their tours, like Hamilton, like DoubtFire. There's also some dates here for wicked and Beetlejuice, which we knew was going to have a non equity tour after its little tiny stop back to Broadway. I'm curious with what the non equity tour set is going to look like for Beetlejuice. I thought that they trimmed it down for the Equity Tour really nice, but I imagine the non equity tour is going to be an even smaller set. So curious what it ends up looking like. And I'm not surprised that we don't see a tour date yet in Atlanta for maybe Happy Ending. It did have its pre Broadway try out at the alliance in Atlanta, similar to water for elephants, which we saw got a date in year two of that tour. So I imagine we'll see something similar for maybe Happy ending. Overall, this is a really solid season. I'm excited to see a lot of these, and maybe I'll see some of them in Atlanta.
